issues: Nothing in the diff gets around the measurement. It uses no file or network access, pastes no answers and uses no test labels. The base model is fit only on (train_smiles, y). The test inputs only pass through phys() and base.predict.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. One method weakness: base_tr comes from in-sample XGB predictions. A tree model fits its own training data more closely than the old Ridge did, so the stage-2 model probably learns from residuals that are too small. This would hurt the candidate, not inflate its score. It fits the worse loss and is not an integrity problem.
The diff calls XGBRegressor but does not add an import. Since the run produced a score, the import must already be in the file.

Check of the numbers: the candidate loss of 0.3824 is 0.0169 worse than the incumbent mean of 0.3655. Using the noise sd of the difference, 0.0037*sqrt(1/1+1/2) ≈ 0.00453, gives |z| ≈ 3.73. The harness reports -3.702. The size agrees within rounding of the means. The negative sign means 'worse' in the harness convention. Using the single-run sd alone would give |z| ≈ 4.57.
The 'reject' decision is right. The candidate is clearly worse than the incumbent.
